messages:
Nia B.: hi all, day 2 here — following the k8s onboarding. I set my context to redwood-staging-oregon but `kubectl get pods -n dev-sandbox` says Forbidden. I did the SSO step. any ideas?

Onboarding Bot: welcome Nia! checklist: `redwoodctl login --sso`, then `redwoodctl sync-kubeconfig --overwrite=false`. Also confirm you don't have multiple kubeconfigs merged in $KUBECONFIG. Docs: https://intranet.redwood/dev-onboarding#k8s

Nia B.: I did redwoodctl login and ran sync-kubeconfig. `echo $KUBECONFIG` -> `/home/nia/.kube/config:/home/nia/.kube/prod`. I thought merging was fine. output: 
```
kubectl config current-context
# => redwood-staging-oregon
kubectl get pods -n dev-sandbox
# Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden: User \"system:anonymous\" cannot list resource \"pods\" in API group \"\" in the namespace \"dev-sandbox\"
```

Raj P.: hey Nia — that anonymous error almost always means kubectl is not authenticating. When KUBECONFIG is a list, kubectl merges them; if an earlier file lacks users/credentials it can lead to anon. Try `KUBECONFIG=/home/nia/.kube/config kubectl auth can-i get pods -n dev-sandbox` to test the single-file config.

Nia B.: `KUBECONFIG=/home/nia/.kube/config kubectl auth can-i get pods -n dev-sandbox` -> "no". weird.

Alex H.: couple of debugging commands to run (mask tokens if pasting):

```
echo $KUBECONFIG
kubectl config view --flatten --minify --raw
kubectl config get-contexts
kubectl config current-context
kubectl --v=6 auth can-i get pods -n dev-sandbox
```

The `--v=6` shows the request headers so you can confirm whether a token is sent.

Nia B.: pasted the outputs privately to Alex — the current context user shows `user: nia@redwood` but the request actually goes without Authorization header. I also noticed `redwood-staging-oregon` context points to cluster entry `staging-oregon` which references an exec plugin `redwoodctl` as the auth provider.

Alex H.: if the exec plugin isn't invoked (eg due to PATH or permissions) you can get anon. Try running `which redwoodctl` and `redwoodctl version`. Also confirm your kubeconfig's exec stanza doesn't have `interactive: false` or bad args. If the exec plugin fails, kubectl falls back to anon.

Nia B.: `which redwoodctl` -> `/usr/local/bin/redwoodctl`. `redwoodctl version` -> v0.9.2. I tried `kubectl --user=nia@redwood --token=REDACTED auth can-i get pods -n dev-sandbox` just to test and it returned "yes" (using a token I grabbed from the synced config).

Raj P.: ok that suggests redwoodctl exec plugin isn't running correctly in the merged config. Workaround: keep per-cluster kubeconfig files and set KUBECONFIG to only the synced file, or run `redwoodctl sync-kubeconfig --cluster=redwood-staging-oregon --out=/home/nia/.kube/staging-config` and then `export KUBECONFIG=/home/nia/.kube/staging-config`. Also file an INFRA ticket so we can check group bindings.

Nia B.: did `redwoodctl sync-kubeconfig --cluster=redwood-staging-oregon --out=/home/nia/.kube/staging-config` and `export KUBECONFIG=/home/nia/.kube/staging-config`. `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n dev-sandbox` -> "no". infra-bot suggested opening a ticket.

infra-bot: Please open a ticket at https://redwood.atlassian.net/jira/projects/INFRA with component "kubernetes" and include your GitHub username. Created INFRA-11021 for niaB.

Nia B.: INFRA-11021 now has my GH handle. quick Q while we wait: are there safer defaults to avoid hitting prod contexts when $KUBECONFIG has many files?

Alex H.: yes — best practices we recommend: 1) keep prod kubeconfigs in a separate file and don't merge, 2) set a non-prod default namespace with `kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=dev-sandbox`, 3) use `kube-ps1` or `kubectl-ps1` in your shell prompt to show current context, 4) alias `k` to `kubectl --context=redwood-staging-oregon` for explicitness when needed. Also `kubectl config view --flatten` can create a single-file view you can inspect.

infra-bot: INFRA-11021 update: verified GH membership for niaB, applied rolebinding `namespace=dev-sandbox role=view subject=group:redwood:devs`. Sync job complete.

Nia B.: ~10m later ran `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n dev-sandbox` -> "yes" and `kubectl get pods -n dev-sandbox` works. resolved. thanks for the context tips, I'll rearrange my kubeconfigs and add a shell prompt indicator.

Raj P.: welcome aboard! small doc suggestion: add a troubleshooting section about exec plugins not firing when kubeconfigs are merged, plus a command snippet to test `kubectl --v=6` for Authorization header.

Nia B.: will do, filing a small PR on the onboarding doc. thanks everyone :tada:
